newsitem.title: USA: Shiva plans sales reorg, closer Nortel tie.
newsitem.headline: Shiva plans sales reorg, closer Nortel tie.

text.p: Shiva Corp said the company's expected earnings shortfall for its recently ended fourth quarter was principally due to weakness in U.S. sales and a key partner's decision to delay an order during the quarter.
In a phone interview, chief financial officer Cynthia Deysher said that, "We didn't receive the Q4 (order) from IBM." IBM Corp is a key reseller of Shiva products.

In addition, Deysher said that, "We didn't ship out as much product as originally planned. Some of that was because we wanted to lower to lower our inventory in the channel. Some of it is we didn't receive all the orders we expected."
Shiva said after the market close Tuesday that it expected earnings for the fourth quarter ended December 28 of $0.05 to $0.07 a share, well below the analyst consensus of $0.21.

To address the shortfall, Deysher said the company planned a series of measures including a reorganziation of its sales force into teams focused on its four core markets: corporate, enterprise, Internet Service Providers and telephone carriers.

In addition, she said Shiva is expanding its strategic relationship with Northern Telecom Ltd. Planned measures include NorTel taking on an increased share of sales expenses and research and development costs of joint efforts.
As part of the arrangement, NorTel will form an internal sales group to boost orders for joint NorTel-Shiva products.

Deysher said the reorganiztion of Shiva's sales organization into teams focused on four market segements differs from the previous structure, which functioned as one large block addressing all potential customers.

Deysher said she expected some of the orders that failed to materialize during the fourth quarter of 1996 to spill over into 1997. "We are expected to grow going forward. I think we are better positioned," she said.
She declined to quantify how much the company might expect to recoup in the first quarter.
Deysher said the slowdown in orders was concentrated in the United States, especially among its "two-tier" distribution partners, which include Ingram Micro Inc, Merisel Inc and Tech Data Corp.
"We had fairly good growth internationally," she noted.

In terms of products, the executive said the major problem was its LAN Rover business, its most mature line of remote access network equipment. She said a LAN Rover product promotion during the quarter failed to meet goals it had set.
In the statement, the company said it expected total revenue for the quarter ending December 28, 1996 to be about $48 to $50 million.

That range would represent a sequential decline from the $57.1 million in revenues reported in Shiva's third quarter ended in September. The company reported $35.6 in revenues for the fourth quarter ended December 30, 1995.
